stem:
I am now convinced, beyond a doubt that unless some great and capital change suddenly takes place . . . this Army must inevitably be reduced to one or other of these three things. Starve, dissolve, or disperse, in order to obtain subsistence in the best manner they can; rest assured Sir this is not an exaggerated picture. . . .

—General George Washington, letter to the Continental Congress, December 23, 1777
instruction: Which of the following prompted General Washington to write this letter?

options.label: F
options.text: A shortage of Continental soldiers to maintain the siege of Yorktown

options.label: G
options.text: The high number of casualties suffered during the Battle of Bunker Hill

options.label: H
options.text: Low morale after the British army captured New York City

options.label: J
options.text: Concern for the Continental troops during the winter at Valley Forge

visual_elements: Text excerpt from General George Washington's letter
Multiple choice options labeled F, G, H, J
